hints: Look at what is being made here, stable combustion products like $\text{CO}_2$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ usually tell you a lot about heat change.
Recall that forming very stable compounds releases a lot of energy, and check which option links to their standard enthalpies of formation.
Remember bond breaking needs energy in while bond making gives energy out, so decide which reason correctly explains a heat-releasing reaction.
walkthrough:
**Spot the type of reaction**

Think of this like burning a fuel. You start with radicals and $\text{NO}_2$ and you make $\text{N}_2$, $\text{CO}_2$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$.

$$4\text{CH}_3\bullet + 7\text{NO}_2 \rightarrow 3\frac{1}{2}\text{N}_2 + 4\text{CO}_2 + 6\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Decide exothermic or endothermic**

Making very stable small molecules like $\text{CO}_2$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ releases far more energy than is needed to break the reactants apart. So heat is given out to the surroundings.

$$\Delta H = \text{energy in (bonds broken)} - \text{energy out (bonds made)} < 0$$

**Choose the correct reason**

$\text{CO}_2$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ have large negative $\Delta H_f^\ominus$ values, meaning huge amounts of energy are released when they form from elements. That dominates the enthalpy change and makes the whole reaction exothermic.

options.A: Endothermic is wrong, this reaction gives out heat. Also, converting chemical energy to heat energy describes what happens in any exothermic change, it does not explain why this one is endothermic.
options.B: Endothermic is wrong. A very high $\text{N}\equiv\text{N}$ bond energy means a lot of energy is released when $\text{N}_2$ forms, which would favour an exothermic change, not an endothermic one.
options.C: Correct. The reaction is exothermic because it produces very stable $\text{CO}_2$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$, which have large negative standard enthalpies of formation. The energy released on forming them outweighs the energy needed to break bonds in reactants.
options.D: Exothermic is the right label but the reason is backwards. Breaking double bonds in $\text{NO}_2$ requires energy input (endothermic step), it cannot by itself explain why the overall reaction releases heat.
